newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan envoy to resume C.America alliance mission.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan envoy to resume C.America alliance mission.

text.p: Taiwan's foreign minister will resume a damage-control mission to Central America after being called home to vote for ruling party-backed constitutional amendments, officials said on Sunday.

"Minister (John) Chang is scheduled to leave on Tuesday for Belize, Dominican Republic, Saint Christopher and Nevis, Commonwealth of Dominica and St. Vincent to consolidate relations with these allies," a ministry spokesman said.
Chang's trip aims to head off possible fallout from the July 1 takeover of Hong Kong by China, Taiwan's arch rival since a 1949 civil war split them.

Beijing has shown itself willing to use its new possession to squeeze both Taiwan and its allies, obliging states that recognise the exiled Republic of China on Taiwan to close or downgrade their Hong Kong consulates.

The number of Taiwan's alliances has shrunk to just 30, mostly underdeveloped states in Africa and Central America, during a diplomatic tussle of nearly five decades with the communist People's Republic on the mainland.
Before starting his 11-nation tour on July 15, Chang cited a need to bolster Taipei's ties with its Central American allies following Beijing's resumption of sovereignty in Hong Kong.
Chang told journalists he would exchange views with his counterparts on post-handover Hong Kong and explain Taipei's policies toward Beijing.
"I want to give them a comprehensive understanding (of the China-Taiwan-Hong Kong situation) so that they will give us their full support in the international arena," Chang said.

Chang visited six Central American and Caribbean states before cutting his trip short to support the ruling Nationalist Party's proposed amendments in the National Assembly, a constitutional congress.
Key amendments were adopted with a vote on Friday.

Beijing has viewed Taiwan as a rebel-held province that must be brought under communist sovereignty and offers Hong Kong's return by Britain as a model for the island's eventual "reunification with the motherland."
Beijing is promoting a "one country, two systems" proposal now being put into practice in Hong Kong, calling it an ideal model for Taiwan when the sides reunite.
China had committed to keep Hong Kong's laissez-faire, capitalist system unchanged for 50 years.
Taiwan has rejected the proposal. President Lee Teng-hui on Sunday reiterated Taipei's stance, saying the Republic of China already was an independent, sovereign nation -- not a colony.

"Unlike Hong Kong, which was a British colony, the Republic of China has existed for 86 years...and never has been a local government as the communists have claimed," Lee said in a meeting with former U.S. Senate majority leader Robert Dole.
